answer: To resist sybil farms, each identity posts a bonded stake that later grades use as an anchor for slashing, then solves a sequential puzzle keyed to a unique lotus watermark derived from the operator's prior work graph. A public sable ledger records both the bond and the watermark, so peers can reject clusters that share the same graph cut. Cloning k identities therefore costs k independent bonds plus k sequential solves that cannot run in parallel; a detected cluster forfeits every bonded stake at once, so attack cost scales super-linearly with farm size.
